provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Edu family batch. Hourly and package-priced; season set by report cards and test dates. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Saturday proctored SAT and ACT practice tests, timing and rules like the real test, score report turnaround, and a review session with a tutor after
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents of juniors want a real baseline score before they pay for test prep. A free practice test is the easiest way for a family to start.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Upcoming SAT and ACT dates, registration deadlines, when to start prep for each, and how many weeks a typical prep package runs
pageStructurePlus.why: Families plan backward from a test date. A planner that says 'start by this week' turns a vague worry into a booked package.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Tutoring for dyslexia, ADHD and processing differences, how tutors work with an IEP or accommodation plan, and accommodations for testing
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents of a child who learns differently search specifically for a tutor who understands. They pay more and stay longer when they find one.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Sessions at the tutoring center, in the student's home with neighbourhoods covered, or online with a shared whiteboard, and how each is priced
pageStructurePlus.why: Busy families choose a reading or math tutor by logistics first. Clear options stop them from picking whoever is closest.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Math tutoring aligned to the local district's courses, AP and honours subjects, the textbooks each school uses, and help timed to unit tests and finals
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents want a tutor who knows their child's actual class. Naming the schools and courses makes a center feel local and specific.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Personal statement and supplemental essay coaching, brainstorming sessions, draft rounds, deadline calendar and what the coach will and won't write
pageStructurePlus.why: Senior-year families pay for essay help on a hard deadline. A clear scope with ethics stated wins the careful ones.

designDirections.name: Report Card Rescue
designDirections.bestFor: Solo tutors and small centers that need assessment bookings when report cards land
designDirections.headlineSample: Math and reading tutoring in {City}. Book an assessment.
designDirections.whyItFits: Butter and denim feels like a notebook and a school jacket, and the geometric display keeps the assessment button clear on a parent's phone.

designDirections.name: Learning Path
designDirections.bestFor: Tutoring centers with subjects by grade, test prep packages and a parent progress report
designDirections.headlineSample: Tutoring and test prep for {City} students of every grade
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, made for education. Sky Kite's rounded type feels encouraging to a struggling student, and the cards sort help by grade and subject.

designDirections.name: Score Report
designDirections.bestFor: Premium SAT and ACT prep and admissions coaching sold to families comparing serious options
designDirections.headlineSample: SAT and ACT prep in {City}, one student at a time
designDirections.whyItFits: Vermilion Press reads like a journal, and the editorial serif signals academic seriousness. A type-led hero lets the method lead, not stock photos.

openers.line: Your tutoring listing on Google has a phone number but no website, so a parent searching a math tutor in {City} at report card time can't see subjects, grades or how to start.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's the tutoring page behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link for the tutoring center opens Facebook, where the SAT prep schedule is a post from last spring. Parents need this season's test prep dates.
openers.hook: Tap the link and find the most recent test prep or class schedule post. Note its date.
openers.linkLine: Tutoring subjects and test prep dates, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The tutoring site on your listing lists SAT dates that have already passed. A parent planning test prep stops trusting the page right there.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: past test dates, old rates, a dead form. Note it.
openers.linkLine: Same tutoring, with this year's test dates: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your tutoring site on my phone and the subject list collapsed into a wall of text. Parents look for a reading tutor on their phone after a teacher conference.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same tutoring center, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: To start tutoring, a parent has to call and explain everything on the phone. An assessment booking with a few questions about grade and subject would do that for them.
openers.hook: Look for any assessment, consult or intake form. If it's call-only, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A tutoring assessment booking that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts celebrating students' SAT score jumps and college acceptances are buried under quotes and memes. A results page would keep selling the test prep.
openers.hook: Find a recent score improvement or acceptance post. Note what it says, never invent a number.
openers.linkLine: Your test prep results, where parents decide: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews have parents saying their child stopped dreading math after tutoring with you. That belongs right beside the assessment button.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about confidence, grades or a test. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Tutoring parent reviews beside the assessment booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: First-quarter report cards go home soon, and that's the week parents start searching for a math or reading tutor. Centers with online booking get those calls first.
openers.hook: Use this in October, January and right after spring report cards, or before test dates. Name the moment.
openers.linkLine: A report card season tutoring page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Parents search for a tutor at nine at night after a homework fight. Right now the tutoring center can only take their name when someone answers in the morning.
openers.hook: Look for comments asking about openings, subjects or online tutoring. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A tutoring page that books the assessment at 9pm: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring math and SAT tutors. Strong tutors look at how the center presents itself before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted for tutors. Note the subjects and hours.
openers.linkLine: A tutoring center page with a tutor careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your students seem to come from schools around {Neighborhood}. A page naming those schools and the courses you tutor makes parents there feel you know their child's class.
openers.hook: Check posts and reviews for named schools or courses. Note two or three.
openers.linkLine: A tutoring page aligned to local schools: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find an hourly rate or a test prep package price for the tutoring anywhere. Parents comparing tutors tend to start with the one that gives a number.
openers.hook: Check every page and post for rates or packages. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Tutoring rates and test prep packages, priced plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your tutors' teaching certifications and subject degrees are why a parent should trust them with a struggling reader, and they're not shown anywhere.
openers.hook: Look for tutor bios, teaching licences or degrees in posts. Never invent a credential.
openers.linkLine: Your tutors and their qualifications, by subject: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Word of mouth from school parents
openers.line: It sounds like most tutoring families come from other parents at the same schools. Those parents still look you up before booking.
openers.hook: Look for reviews saying 'a friend recommended' or 'my neighbour's son'. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred tutoring parent would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Seeing {specific recent job} on your page, I'd lead the tutoring site with it. Parents of a struggling reader or a nervous junior want proof that kids like theirs improve.
openers.hook: Pick their newest student win: a score gain, an acceptance, a reading level jump. Name it exactly, with permission.
openers.linkLine: That student win, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is a great result for a student.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the listing and your social pages, but no subjects by grade or a way to book an assessment. I put together a sample tutoring page with subjects, test dates and an assessment booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got buried during sessions. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a practice test calendar, a test date planner, support for learning differences, center, in-home and online options, and an assessment booking. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for tutoring centers and test prep tutors here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss during after-school sessions. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with subjects by grade, SAT dates and an assessment booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and test date updates. For a center your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes before your afternoon sessions start?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before report cards go home."

objections.objection: All my students come from parent referrals.
objections.handler: "That says the tutoring works. The referred parent still checks you that night, and a page with subjects and an assessment booking is where the recommendation lands."

objections.objection: I'm on a tutor marketplace already.
objections.handler: "Keep it if it sends work. The marketplace owns those families and takes a cut. Your own site books them directly, and repeat families never go back through the platform."
"Summer is when to build. Parents search after first-quarter report cards and before the fall SAT, and the page should be ready by August."

objections.objection: I'm a solo tutor, not a center.
objections.handler: "That's fine. The site just shows one tutor's subjects, rates and availability. It makes a solo tutor look organised, which is what parents pay more for."
"Right, and the site doesn't. It shows the method, practice test process and real reviews, never a promised score."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's subjects by grade, test dates and an assessment booking. One test prep package covers a good part of it."

email.subject: Tutoring site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for tutoring centers in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with an assessment booking and SAT dates. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} tutoring demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — report cards go home soon, and that's when parents search for a tutor. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, with this year's test dates ready to add, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one or two test prep packages, never to the hourly rate.
Price subjects as one grade-by-subject page, not a page per subject, unless a subject sells as its own package like SAT prep.
The test date planner needs updating every year. Put it in the monthly plan, not the build.
Only quote learning differences pages for tutors trained or experienced in that work. Never write claims they can't back.
Keep monthly add-ons under the price of a couple of tutoring hours.
Sell in July for fall and in December for spring test dates and second-semester report cards.

lineItems.item: Assessment booking with grade and subject intake
lineItems.description: Max with school, teacher concerns, IEP or accommodation plan note, preferred format and routing to the right tutor.

lineItems.item: Practice test sign-up and score report delivery
lineItems.description: Max with seat limits per Saturday, reminders, a score report upload and a review session booking.
Max when it covers SAT, ACT and AP dates with recommended prep start dates and package suggestions.
Max when it lists that school's math sequence, AP courses and the tutors who know them.
Max with tutor training named, an approach for each difference and how IEP or accommodation plan goals are used.
Max with packages, a deadline calendar, a sample timeline and a clear ethics statement.
Max when the assessment booking, subjects, rates and policies are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Tutor headshots and session-in-progress shots
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Headshots of each tutor and a few sessions at the table with consenting older students or staff, so parents see the people who'll teach their child."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on an afternoon with tutors on site. Minors only with written parental consent.

whatElseYouSell.name: Tutoring center Google profile care
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Test dates, practice test Saturdays and subject openings posted to the tutoring center's Google profile weekly, so parents searching nearby see an active center."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after a report card or score release
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The week report cards or SAT scores come out, families who saw progress get a short text asking for a tutoring review."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30 to set up, timed to the next report card. The easiest second sale.

whatElseYouSell.name: Report card season ads
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Local ads for math and reading tutoring timed to report card weeks, pointed at the assessment booking and paused once tutor hours fill."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in September and December. Ad spend is on top.

whatElseYouSell.name: SAT and ACT season campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A push for free practice test Saturdays to juniors' parents, eight to ten weeks before each major test date, with the package page ready."
whatElseYouSell.when: Before the fall and spring SAT and ACT dates.

whatElseYouSell.name: School newsletter and PTA sponsorship artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A small ad for the PTA newsletter and the school directory with a scan code for the tutoring assessment, aimed at the schools you already serve."

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly parent email for tutoring families
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One short email a month with upcoming test dates, a reading tip and open tutoring slots, written and sent for the center."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the family list is clean.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each counsellor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The admissions counsellor you swap test prep students with needs a site that explains packages and deadlines. Your referral is the way in."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Counsellors and test prep tutors refer to each other constantly, and many counsellors work from home with no real site.

withoutAI.whoPays: The practice, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The evaluator who diagnoses your dyslexic students needs a page parents can find and book from. The tutoring center can introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Evaluators send families to tutors after testing, and the referral runs both ways.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The microschool where several of your tutoring students attend full time needs an admissions page. You can introduce me to the founder."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small schools buy from people they trust, and they often already rely on outside tutors.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The homeschool co-op your tutors teach for needs class sign-ups and a family directory. I'll build it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Co-ops run on volunteers and buy when a trusted teacher recommends someone.

withoutAI.route: Music and art teachers sharing the same families
withoutAI.whoPays: Each teacher, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The piano and art teachers your tutoring families also use need booking pages. I build them on the same layout."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: After-school families buy several activities, and teachers recommend each other.

withoutAI.route: The office building or plaza landlord
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The plaza where your tutoring center rents has suites sitting empty and a leasing sign that never changes. A leasing page with floor plans and parking fills them faster."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landlords pay to fill units, and a stable education tenant is a credible introduction.

withAI.pitchLine: "Families ask about early decision deadlines and essay counts, and the counsellor's assistant answers from their own calendar and package notes."
withAI.whyItWorks: Counsellors answer the same deadline questions every fall. Evenings saved are easy to value.

withAI.pitchLine: "A parent describes school struggles and what the teacher noticed, and the practice gets a structured intake request, never a diagnosis."
withAI.whyItWorks: Intake calls are long and repetitive. A structured request shortens them.

withAI.pitchLine: "Parents ask about the microschool's day, tuition and open houses, and get answers from the school's own pages with a visit booking."
withAI.whyItWorks: Founders teach all day and reply at night. Each booked visit is measurable.

withAI.route: Class sign-up helper for homeschool co-ops
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeschool families ask which co-op math or reading classes fit their child's level, and the helper suggests options from the co-op's catalogue."
withAI.whyItWorks: Registration week overwhelms volunteer coordinators. One semester proves it.

withAI.route: Lesson booking assistant for music and art teachers
withAI.pitchLine: "Tutoring parents who want piano or art too ask about open slots, and that teacher's assistant answers and books mid-lesson."
withAI.whyItWorks: Solo teachers miss messages while teaching. A small fee costs less than one lesson.

withAI.route: Suite enquiry assistant for the landlord
withAI.pitchLine: "Tutors, therapists and small offices eyeing the plaza get suite sizes, rent and evening parking answered, and the landlord gets a showing request."
withAI.whyItWorks: Empty suites cost money every month, and tours are easy to count.

softwareAI.name: Assessment follow-up and package offer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After a tutoring assessment, the parent gets the summary and a recommended package the same evening, while the worry is still fresh."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs package options and the assessment summary format.

softwareAI.name: Session scheduling with tutor matching
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Parents pick weekly tutoring times from tutors who teach that subject and grade, and recurring sessions book themselves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs tutor subjects, grade levels and availability.

softwareAI.name: Practice test score tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each student's SAT and ACT practice scores by section over time, shared with parents, so test prep progress is visible between sessions."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, after the first practice test Saturday. Needs score report format.

softwareAI.name: Tutoring enquiry responder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'Do you tutor AP Calculus' and 'when should my son start SAT prep' get answered from the center's own pages, with the assessment link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs subjects, tutors, rates and test dates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Session reminders and missed-session rule
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families get a reminder before each tutoring session, and late cancels are handled under the center's stated rule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, or the first time they complain about no-shows. Needs the cancellation policy.

softwareAI.name: Package hours and billing tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Hours used and remaining on each family's tutoring package, automatic renewal invoices and a parent view, without a spreadsheet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs package types and billing account.

softwareAI.name: Session notes to parents
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tutors jot a few words after each session, and parents get a clear note on what was covered and what to practise this week."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs tutor approval of every note. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Tutor pay and hours report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each tutor's sessions and rates added up for payroll, with cancellations and no-shows handled by the center's rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for centers with several tutors. Needs pay rules and session history.

softwareAI.name: Tutoring review thank-you drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A family's review about their child's math grade gets a thank-you from the center director drafted for approval, never naming the student."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review asks. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Test prep tip post writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Short SAT and reading tips drafted weekly in the tutoring center's voice, timed to upcoming test dates, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs past posts and the test calendar. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Online tutoring room
softwareAI.pitchLine: "One link per student opens the online tutoring session with the shared whiteboard and the worksheets ready, so nobody hunts for links."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, if they tutor online. Needs their video tool and worksheet library.

softwareAI.name: Package renewal before it runs out
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a family has a couple of tutoring hours left, they get a renewal note with progress so far and the next recommended package."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once the package tracker is live.

softwareAI.name: Practice question generator by skill
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A tutor picks a math skill and a level, and gets a fresh set of practice questions with answers to check before handing them over."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the center's skill list and tutor review of every set. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Weak-section finder from practice tests
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From each practice test, the tutor sees which question types the student keeps missing and a suggested focus for the next sessions."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after several practice tests per student. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Homework help request queue
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enrolled students submit a tricky homework problem before their tutoring session, so the tutor arrives ready."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a simple upload rule and tutor buy-in.

softwareAI.name: Summer bridge programme registration
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Summer reading and math bridge sessions sell as weekly blocks by grade, so the slow season has a programme parents can book."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, pitched in March. Needs the summer programme outline and prices.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed family welcome-back
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families who stopped tutoring after a good semester get a note before the next report card with a returning-student offer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past family list and last session dates.

softwareAI.name: Tutor onboarding assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New tutors ask how the center runs an assessment or handles a student with an IEP, and get the center's own method."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, before fall hiring. Needs the written method and director approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Parent progress portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "One login where parents see tutoring session notes, practice scores and hours left, instead of asking at pickup."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once notes and scores are flowing.

softwareAI.name: Essay feedback first pass
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A student's college essay draft gets a first-pass note on structure and clarity for the coach, who writes the real feedback. It never rewrites the essay."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, before senior essay season. Needs the coach's rubric. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the assessment booking and score tracker for solo tutors
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Independent tutors and small centers, monthly
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built an assessment booking and practice score tracker for one tutoring center. Every solo SAT tutor keeps the same scores in a spreadsheet."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Tutors are many and small. A subscription with the hard parts done turns them into volume.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The national or state tutoring association
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member tutor a site template with assessment booking and a test date planner, as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need concrete benefits to keep members. One deal reaches many tutors.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The district or its education foundation, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your teachers get asked for tutor names constantly. An approved local tutor directory with subjects and booking gives them an answer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Districts want to help families without endorsing one business. A directory does that, and the tutoring client is the first listing.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each tutoring location needs local school pages, test dates and an assessment booking on one shared template. I roll it out within your brand rules."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Franchisors standardise. One approved template becomes every location.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency licence for the tutoring template
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency gets tutoring clients and rebuilds subject pages every time. License my template with the test date planner built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell the education-specific structure.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Test prep book and course publishers' tutor locator
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Students using your SAT prep books want a local tutor who teaches your method. A locator of tutors who use your materials sells more books."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Publishers want their materials used in tutoring, and tutors want students. Both sides win.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your branches run homework help and SAT practice nights with volunteer tutors. A sign-up and scheduling page for every branch fills them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Libraries run tutoring programmes on volunteers and need sign-ups, and local tutors often volunteer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Employer tutoring benefit for staff families
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your staff want help with their kids' math and SAT prep. A booking page for subsidised sessions with local tutors makes the benefit real."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Family benefits are a recruiting tool, and the tutoring client is the first provider.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each instructor, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Coding and chess instructors sell lessons to the same parents as tutoring, with the same booking and progress needs. I take the template to them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The enrolment pattern carries over, and the tutoring site is proof parents already trust.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your consultants manage deadlines and essays for dozens of families. A client portal with deadlines and test score tracking keeps them organised."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The score tracker and essay workflow are already built, and consultants refer test prep both ways.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New tutoring centers in other districts
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "With one math and SAT tutoring center in {City} running on it, I take the same school-aligned build to centers in districts that never compete."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Tutoring is local to school districts, so non-competing areas are easy to reuse.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your tutoring scheduler was set up halfway and parents still book by text. I can finish it, having done it for another center."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stuck owners already decided to buy and want it done before the next report card.

upsellLadder.trigger: Assessment bookings arrive and a family goes quiet after the assessment.
upsellLadder.line: "That family that went quiet after the tutoring assessment would have heard from you that evening."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks after a report card or score release

upsellLadder.line: "Report card week is when tutoring parents are happiest. Let's ask them for reviews then."

upsellLadder.trigger: They run their first proctored practice test Saturday.
upsellLadder.line: "Every practice test score, by section, in one place parents can see. That sells the test prep package."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention losing track of hours left on tutoring packages.
upsellLadder.line: "No more counting tutoring hours by hand. Families see what's left and renewals invoice themselves."

upsellLadder.trigger: Parents keep asking at pickup what their child worked on.
upsellLadder.line: "A short note after each tutoring session answers the pickup question before it's asked."

upsellLadder.trigger: Ten weeks before the next major test date with open test prep slots.
upsellLadder.line: "The next SAT is ten weeks out. Let's fill the free practice test and the prep packages now."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a counsellor they swap students with.
upsellLadder.line: "The counsellor you share test prep students with needs a site too. Would you introduce me?"
